To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a significant fraction of HIV-infected persons produce TGF-β in response to stimulation by HIV proteins, and the TGF- β-producing cells can nonspecifically inhibit both HIV- and unrelated virus-specific CTL responses.

a subset of CD8+ T cell clones from HIV-infected donors produce TGF-β in response to stimulation by HIV proteins and peptides, and that TGF-β suppresses the IFN- γ response of CD8 + T cell clones to HIV proteins and peptides.
∼25-50% of HIV-specific CD8+ T cell responses are immunoregulatory in HIV-infected individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
HIV-specific CD8+ T cell response and its relationship with the HIV infection.
the mechanisms by which HIV infection induces a state of immunosuppression that contributes to the progression to AIDS.
the role of TGF- β1 in HIV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIV infection induces a population of TGF- β1-producing CD8+ T lymphocytes that can suppress HIV-specific and unrelated CD8+ T cell immune responses.
TGF-β-producing cells are not a major cause of the loss of CTL function in HIV-infected individuals.
HIV antigens can induce TGF-β producing immunoregulatory CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cell, and NK cells, which can suppress the HIV-specific CTL responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-infected individuals can produce TGF-β in response to stimulation of HIV proteins or peptides, and that this production can nonspecifically reduce the IFNγ production of CD8+ T lymphocytes.
HIV antigens can induce TGF-β-producing CD8+ T cell clones that can nonspecifically inhibit both HIV-specific and non-HIV-specific CTL responses.
the HIV-specific CD8+ T cell response is not a simple binary on/off response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV-specific CD8+ T-cell responses can be suppressed by HIV antigens through a TGF-β-mediated mechanism.
TGF-β is an important immunosuppressive factor in HIV infection, and it can be produced by CD8+ T lymphocytes.
HIV proteins can induce the production of TGF-b1 by CD8+ T lymphocytes, which can suppress HIV- and vaccinia-specific IFN-gamma production by CD8+ lymphocytes.
